title: Frontend: Detect Cycle in an Undirected Connected Graph (DFS)
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Detect Cycle in an Undirected Connected Graph (DFS). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({count,edges}). Return whether an undirected graph has a cycle; include disconnected components, self-loops, and parallel edges. Track incoming edge identity rather than only parent vertex.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
In a simple graph DFS, an already visited neighbor that is not the current node’s parent indicates a cycle.
alternativeApproaches: Produce the actual cycle path and explain how edge identity changes multigraph detection.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Tree; triangle; self-loop.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
